# How to Increase Restaurant Sales: 10 Proven Strategies

Full on Fridays, quiet on Tuesdays? If your restaurant revenue isn't where it should be, you're not alone — and the problem is almost never the food.

[Growth](https://sell.glovoapp.com/ug/en/resources/news?category=growth)21/07/2026

![](https://glovo.dhmedia.io/image/vrm-self-signup/landing-pages/glovo-sell/restaurant_sales_en-e1784624088534.jpeg)

Most restaurants are making the same fixable mistakes: invisible online, menus that don’t convert, and nothing to bring customers back. All of that is solvable.

Here are **10 strategies that actually work**. 👇

## **1️⃣ Fix your online presence before anything else**

70% of customers check a restaurant online before deciding where to order or eat. If your restaurant does not show up in a search, **you do not exist for that customer**.

Start with the basics: make sure your restaurant is listed on Google Maps with accurate opening hours, a phone number, and photos. Add your menu. Respond to reviews. This costs nothing and makes an immediate difference.

If you are not on any food delivery app yet, this is the single biggest gap you can close. Customers who want to order from home will not call — they will open an app.

## **2️⃣ Make your menu work harder**

Most restaurant menus are too long. A menu with 40 items does not give customers more choice — it gives them decision fatigue. They end up ordering the safest thing, **not the most profitable one**.

Audit your menu. Identify your three to five best-selling, highest-margin dishes. Give them better names and descriptions. Add photos where possible. Move them to the top.

Cut dishes that rarely sell. A shorter menu is cheaper to run, reduces waste, and makes it easier for delivery platforms to promote your best items.

## **3️⃣ Use promotions strategically, not constantly**

Use promotions to solve a specific problem: fill slow hours, introduce a new dish, reward loyal customers.

A happy hour promotion from 2pm to 5pm on weekdays can turn dead hours into productive ones. A free side dish for orders over a certain amount increases average order value without cutting your margin on the main dish.

**The key is having a clear goal for every promotion**. If you cannot say what problem it solves, do not run it.

## **4️⃣ Build a base of returning customers**

**Getting a new customer costs five times more than keeping one**. Your most valuable customers are the people who already love your food — and you probably do not have a system to stay in their minds.

The simplest retention tool is a loyalty stamp card. But if you are on a delivery platform, you can use that platform’s tools to offer repeat customers a reason to come back — a discount on their next order, a free item after five purchases.

Even something as simple as remembering a regular customer’s usual order builds the kind of loyalty that no promotion can buy.

## **5️⃣ Get serious about your delivery channel**

Delivery is no longer a nice-to-have. In most urban markets, it now represents 30 to 50 percent of total restaurant revenue. **If you are treating your delivery channel as secondary, you are leaving real money behind**.

Delivery sales require a different approach than dine-in. Your packaging needs to travel well. Your menu needs to feature items that hold up over 20 minutes. Your photos need to sell the dish before the customer ever tastes it.

Treat your delivery presence the way you treat your physical restaurant: invest in presentation, respond to ratings, and track which dishes perform best.

## **6️⃣ Price your menu correctly**

Many restaurant owners underprice their food because they are afraid to lose customers. But customers who leave because of a fair price increase were not loyal customers — they were bargain hunters.

**Review your food cost percentage**. If your ingredients cost more than 30 to 35 percent of your menu price, your margins are under pressure. A small price adjustment on your most popular dishes often has less impact on volume than you expect, while significantly improving your bottom line.

## **7️⃣ Photograph your food properly**

One good photo of your best dish will do more for your sales than a week of social media posts about nothing specific.

You do not need a professional photographer. You need a clean plate, natural daylight from a window, and a phone. Shoot from above or at a 45-degree angle. No filters. No dark backgrounds. Food should look fresh, appetising, and real.

Update your photos on every platform you are on — Google, your delivery apps, your own social media. Outdated photos of dishes you no longer serve are actively hurting you.

## **8️⃣ Train your team to sell**

**Your staff are your best sales tool** and most restaurants never train them to sell. Suggesting a side dish, recommending a drink pairing, or mentioning a dessert are not pushy — they are good service.

A simple daily briefing — this is today’s special, this is what we are trying to move, these are the three dishes we are most proud of right now — gives your team the information they need to sell without feeling scripted.

## **9️⃣ Track your numbers weekly**

You cannot improve what you do not measure. At minimum, track your weekly revenue, your average order value, and your table or order turnover.

If you are on a delivery platform, **check your weekly reports**. Which dishes have the highest ratings? Which ones get the most complaints? Where are customers dropping off before completing an order?

These numbers tell you exactly where your revenue is leaking. Most of the time, fixing two or three things makes a significant difference.

## **🔟 Show up where your customers already are**

Your customers are on Instagram, on WhatsApp groups, and on food delivery apps. **If your restaurant is not visible in those places, a competitor’s is**.

# Glovo 101: Guide, Tips, and Key Points for Your Restaurant’s Success on Glovo (2023)

Glovo is a delivery platform available in 26 countries, known for its food delivery from restaurants and ghost kitchens. Here we share the key points for registering your restaurant and tips for maximizing its potential.

*   [What should be taken into account before starting to use a delivery platform?](https://www.deliverect.com/en-mx/blog/online-food-delivery/glovo-101-the-essential-guide-for-restaurants#section-what-should-be-taken-into-account-before-starting-to-use-a-delivery-platform)

As the owner of a restaurant or ghost kitchen, your tasks frequently include navigating a sea of digital options to select one or more touchpoints to offer your menu to reach more customers and increase sales.

The online food ordering and delivery platforms market is expanding. In 2021, data estimated its [**global value at USD 189.70 billion**](https://www.grandviewresearch.com/industry-analysis/online-food-delivery-market-report). This trend is expected to continue, particularly in an increasingly digital world where nearly [**6 billion people own smartphones.**](https://www.statista.com/statistics/330695/number-of-smartphone-users-worldwide/)

This scenario encourages you to keep navigating to find new customers, make connections, and, most importantly, create new relationships between your menu and diners. As a result, **it is crucial to understand how food delivery platforms such as Glovo work.**

## **What is Glovo?**

According to the platform, Glovo is a Spanish company that was established in 2014. It currently operates in 26 countries and 200 cities, with a total of 5.1 million active users.

Glovo is an online platform that provides home delivery services for food from restaurants and ghost kitchens. They recently announced the sale of their operations in Latin America, where they had a presence in eight countries. Currently, they are mainly focusing on Europe, where they are leaders in Spain, but they also have a presence in some countries in Africa and Asia.

> We’re a Spanish tech company and the fastest-growing multicate
